text:
maya: Heads up — we saw a cascade of evictions yesterday when a hosted burst pool prewarmed nodes and an AZ-wide networking flap increased conntrack pressure. Pods running in tenant namespaces that were supposed to be isolated ended up on the same burst nodes and hit NAT timeouts.
raj: ugh. Which routing path? was it egress via shared NAT gateway?
maya: yeah, shared NAT in that AZ. The autoscaler spun up burst nodes (label: pool=hosted-burst) that accept both hosted and dedicated workloads because of permissive tolerations.
sam: can we enforce namespace -> pool affinity via an admission webhook? basically deny tolerations for hosted pools if namespace has annotation dedicated=true
li: that's doable. but we also need a fallback for legitimate bursts (e.g., dedicated tenants allowed to burst but keep network isolation). we can't break bursts entirely.
maya: proposal: namespace "lease banking" — namespaces get a small reserved slot on dedicated pools and a separate soft-quarantine burst pool when they exceed it. soft-quarantine pool uses strict egress SNAT per-namespace (different NAT IPs) and stricter conntrack settings.
raj: sketch of implementation?
maya: 1) admission webhook enforces nodeSelector/toleration policy by namespace annotation. 2) autoscaler rules create ephemeral node pools with taint: quarantine=true:NoSchedule. 3) burst controller can create a per-namespace kube-proxy/SNAT config or attach an ip-per-pod CNI profile. 4) cost accounting updates to charge burst usage to namespace's billing tag.
sam: sounds heavy but manageable. can we prototype with taints + a binding controller first? simpler: mutation webhook adds nodeAffinity + toleration to pods from tenant namespaces so they never land on hosted-burst nodes unless explicitly allowed.
li: agree on incremental approach. start with mutation webhook + E2E test. if a pod needs to opt into hosted-burst then set annotation: example.com/allow-hosted-burst=true and we gate that on quota/billing.
maya: here's a minimal mutating webhook patch example we can use in tests:```yamlapiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1kind: MutatingWebhookConfigurationmetadata:name: tenant-pool-mutatewebhooks: - name: tenant-pool.example.com  clientConfig:    service:      name: pool-guard      namespace: infra      path: "/mutate"  rules:  - operations: ["CREATE"]    apiGroups: [""]    apiVersions: ["v1"]    resources: ["pods"]``` It injects:```yamlspec:  affinity:    nodeAffinity:      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:        nodeSelectorTerms:        - matchExpressions:          - key: pool-type            operator: In            values: ["dedicated", "soft-quarantine"]  tolerations:  - key: "quarantine"    operator: "Exists"    effect: "NoSchedule"```
raj: nice. Also add a check in scheduler profiles to prefer same-namespace packing to reduce cross-tenant node siblings. that will lower noisy-neighbor effects.
li: ops question: how do we ensure cost visibility? need to emit prometheus metrics for leased slots: tenant_leases{namespace="foo"} and burst_charge{namespace="foo",pool="soft-quarantine"} so billing can pick it up.
sam: add an alert: if conntrack_established_per_node > 80% on nodes labeled pool=hosted-burst then scale down and failover to dedicated/soft-quarantine. maybe a circuit breaker.
oncall-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026 - AZ-burst-nat-saturation (see runbook link) :eyes:
maya: I'll put a short RFC in eng-infra/google-docs with the incremental plan (mutating webhook -> prototype -> metrics -> admission + autoscaler hooks). tagging @raj @sam to review.
raj: :thumbsup: please include testcases: evict/scale/conntrack spikes and billing attribution.
li: I'll pair on the first-day prototype.
maya: thanks — starting PR for the webhook mock tomorrow.
